title: A site wearing no design system is told its template's role variables and that a new element copies the template's own kind; the slot read returns the template's role fallbacks, which judge EmDash rebuild pins, page.look pins and the WordPress/Joomla literals a look write typed over a role, with the template's value as the fallback
steps: S1: No stand, no browser, no model. In the TCH checkout at the commit under test, with dependencies installed (pnpm install), run: node --test --test-reporter=tap packages/tools/tracy-site-tools/test/role-pins.test.mjs packages/tools/tracy-site-tools/test/role-pins-bash.test.mjs packages/tools/tracy-site-tools/test/ds-slot-worn.test.mjs packages/tools/tracy-site-tools/test/ds-slot-wiring.test.mjs packages/tools/tracy-site-tools/test/look-set.test.mjs packages/tools/tracy-site-tools/test/read-compact.test.mjs packages/site/tracy-site-build-emdash/test/slot-pins.test.mjs
S2: Record the exit code, '# fail' and the result of each test named in run.tests.
expect: designLine(null, null, {platform}) on emdash, wordpress and joomla starts '- Design system: none worn — the site shows its template's own look.', names `--ds-c-{bg,surface,…}`, `--ds-{btn,card,input,pill}-radius`, `--ds-font-{display,body,…}` and the status colours, says 'never a bare hex, font name or radius, asked or not' and 'A NEW element (button, card, section) copies the classes of the template's own element of that kind', carries no hex, ≤ 1400 bytes; a bound record keeps its own line first; a worn slot still wins; a worn slot's line carries the same new-element sentence.

siteContext: slot null (the read found none) on an installed site → the roles line, and nothing else in the block changes; slot undefined (the read did not answer) → no design line, as before; an imported site → no role line; an agent step whose slot read printed {ok:true, css:null} carries the 'none worn' line.

templateRolesOf on a template stylesheet: each role's most frequent fallback, a fallback through the template's own variable resolved (var(--ds-c-accent, var(--k-primary)) → #a3e635); a stylesheet reading no role → null. nearestRoles picks by paint first and names every role at the shortest distance (#14171a as text → --ds-c-fg and --ds-c-heading).

rolePins, nothing worn: a WordPress button block typed with background #a3e635, colour #0b0f0a, radius 8px (block attributes and inline style) is answered with background(-color): var(--ds-c-accent, #a3e635), color: var(--ds-c-accent-on, #0b0f0a), border-radius: var(--ds-btn-radius, 8px); next says a design system the customer applies later will not reach them and a value the customer named exactly may stay. Worn: the worn system's orange copied off the page → var(--ds-c-accent, #a3e635), the TEMPLATE's value as the fallback; nothing worn, the literal itself is the fallback. var()/presets/layout/keywords/the slot's own sheet pass; a template variable set to a literal is named.
The EmDash read script, run by node on a fixture /app: with no slot it answers css null and roles from /app/src (node_modules skipped); with a slot it answers the slot and the same roles.

EmDash slot-pins, nothing worn: the read returns the template stylesheets as roles; a new 'btn-primary rounded-full bg-[#da5a2a] text-[#14171a]' → rounded-[var(--ds-btn-radius,9999px)], bg-[var(--ds-c-accent,#da5a2a)], and both --ds-c-fg and --ds-c-heading for the shared ink; pinsNext(pins, false) says a design system applied later will not reach them; rebuildSite answers those findings; a template that reads no role reads nothing.

page.look with the template's roles: a literal row gets 'a literal over the template's role --ds-c-fg or --ds-c-heading: a design system applied later will not reach it — write …'; a row set through a role gets none.

look.set on WordPress/Joomla, scope site, a token the slot sets: refused as the system's own; next says a change of degree is written relative to the slot's variable (calc(var(--…) + 4px)) and only a value the customer named exactly is written as named.

A bash command that writes a stylesheet: shellLookFiles names every stylesheet each form writes (sed -i files, a > or heredoc target, tee, cp/mv destination, an inline script that opens one for writing) and none it only reads, no compiler, nothing for a command that cannot be split; the read runs by sh from the command's own directory (a missing file, a directory, a file past 256 KB read as null = not checked); newRolePins names only what the new text adds over the old (one rule added to a minified stylesheet → just its literal); wired through tools/execute and the next step: a sed that appends '.cta{background:#a3e635;border-radius:999px}' to the theme's style.css gets the notice 'After your look edit (style.css): … `background: #a3e635` → `background: var(--ds-c-accent, #a3e635)` … `border-radius: 999px` → `border-radius: var(--ds-btn-radius, 999px)` (nothing worn: the literal stays the fallback)', none of the template's own values, the same literal again in the turn is not said twice, and a file the command names that is not there is said as 'Not checked for literals over the design-system roles'.

A site wearing nothing whose template reads no role (Tracy Business EmDash 1.7.4): the line claims no role variable — 'none worn … keep to the template's own classes and variables' plus the new-element rule; a bound record keeps its line, then the new-element rule.

The review of 20/10/2026, each as a case: a colour equal to a role IS that role whatever it paints (#da5a2a as text → --ds-c-accent), a colour farther than 48 from every role of its paint gets none (#ff0000 text, #000 background), a near one keeps its own value as the fallback; a non-button 50%/0/9999px corner is a shape (none), a button's pill is pinned; a face keeps itself as the fallback; worn, the fallback is the template's own value (background → #da5a2a, face → "Inter", sans-serif); a top-level block fontFamily slug, words in a "text" attribute, url(#…) and href="#…" are not literals, inside style.color/typography they are; surface-warm and accent-on-ink can be named; a whole body is judged against the body read; comments are not reads, two-level nested fallbacks are read; the template's light side is a role's value and its dark side (prefers-color-scheme: dark, [data-theme=dark]) only an alternative a literal may match; a file tool's edit names only what it added, never the lines its new_string repeats; the pins are said even when tracy_design_check runs right after; a read before the command that timed out leaves the file not checked, its old literals never named; the EmDash read survives a broken symlink, a folder named *.css and commented reads.

The second review round, each as a case: a dark-side value never crosses paints (dark #111111 as text → --ds-c-fg, never --ds-c-bg); a corner is a button's only when the rule or element it styles is a button (a stylesheet naming .btn elsewhere leaves an avatar's 50% alone), and @font-face faces are not pinned; a key names its own record, a created record is all new, an edited block is judged against the record's body, a read keeps only the body field; only the dark switch is the dark side (not .btn-dark, :root:not(.dark), a mixed list; an unclosed block leaves the rest light); a slot read that did not answer leaves the file not checked; a cd to an unknown place is unresolved and said; missing / not read / too large files are told apart.

The third review round: onRead hears a WordPress read whole before W2 shows the model its outline (so a block edit on a long page is judged), and a listener that throws changes nothing; @font-face after a <style> or a comment is never pinned, commented declarations paint nothing; a light near match of the paint beats any dark value and an unknown paint never reads the dark side; body.is-dark-theme, an all-dark list, [data-color-mode=dark] and a theme.json css string opening dark are the dark side, an unclosed dark block skips itself only; one literal is one pin across a block attribute and its inline style; .btn-group / .wp-block-buttons are not buttons, a tag with > in an attribute and input[type=submit] are read right; a quoted face is read whole; a Joomla call without kind is an article (introtext, fulltext); a cd inside a subshell or a pushd leaves names unresolved; a record written whole without a read, or a site whose slot read did not answer, is said as not checked.

The fourth review round: CSS a heredoc or a sed script carries (calc(…(…)), @media (…), $(…)) never makes a cd unknown, and a cd inside ( … ) ends with the subshell; the whole tag tells the element (a class or type after style=), a child combinator is part of the selector; a quoted value never runs into the next attribute (a changed href does not make an old literal new); only a body field is judged against the body read, a title or status is the write's own and words alone carry nothing to note; /* in markup is not a comment; unclosed dark openers stay bounded (8,000 in under 2 s); the accent is a role for text and lines as well as grounds.
evidence: 20/10/2026: every template now supports changing the design system; a new button must follow the customer's template when no design system is worn, and the new system's rules when one is. Read in the code on develop 86b7e91fee: the slot line exists only while a slot is worn and speaks of editing an existing element; a site wearing none gets no role variable; slot-pins.mjs reads nothing when /app/data/ds-slot.css is absent; WP/Joomla have no pin check; look.set's slot refusal said 'the value they named'.
fence: Mechanism only: what the context says and what the reads, checks and answers name. Not covered: whether the model then writes the var() — that is the stand acceptance (new button, unworn → system A → system B → taken off, three CMS).
